h1: Baptist vs Catholic: what is the difference?
searchTitle: Baptist vs Catholic: The Real Differences, Plainly
description: The Bible and the church, the Mass, baptism and the pope. Where Baptists and Catholics part, in words each side would accept.
answer: Catholics read the Bible inside the church that handed it down, and hold that the bread and wine become Christ's body and blood. Baptists hold to Scripture alone and keep the Supper as a remembrance. Both say God's grace can be refused, and that nobody earns the first move.
drawn: The rails draw the Roman Catholic Church as its Catechism and councils state it, and traditional, non-Calvinist Southern Baptists. Twenty-three Eastern Catholic churches hold the same teaching with different liturgies.
common: Grace comes first and can be refused. The two stand close here: Catholic teaching says nothing at the start is earned, and that the will can say no.
The same creed. Both confess the Trinity, Jesus as God and man, risen bodily. A Baptist reads it off the page; a Catholic as the church always has.
Both take the Bible to be God's own word, without error in what it teaches. The argument is over who settles the meaning.

differences.heading: Who has the last word
differences.a: Baptists hold to Scripture alone, which is a claim about which authority is final rather than a refusal to learn from anybody. Only the Bible is beyond error, any council may be wrong, and nothing can be required as an article of belief that cannot be shown from the text itself. Neither bishop nor council stands over a congregation reading it.
differences.b: Catholics do not set Scripture against tradition; they deny that the question makes sense. Dei Verbum says both flow from the same divine wellspring, and that interpreting them authentically belongs to the church's teaching office, the magisterium. A Catholic meeting a hard passage asks what the church has understood it to mean, and experiences that as the way the Bible is heard.
differences.plain: When a verse is disputed, a Catholic asks what the church has taught; a Baptist asks what the text carries.

differences.heading: The Lord's Supper and baptism
differences.a: Baptists call the Supper an ordinance rather than a sacrament. The bread and cup remember and proclaim Christ's death until He comes, and the blessing comes through the faith of the one taking part rather than through the elements. Baptism is the immersion of someone old enough to say what they believe: a confession of what God has already done.
differences.b: At Mass the bread and wine become the body and blood of Christ. The word for it is transubstantiation: what they look like, taste like and are chemically stays the same; what they are does not. Trent defined it in 1551 and the Catechism repeats it. Infants are baptised, and everything in the building is arranged around the altar where this happens.
differences.plain: One church remembers a death at the Table; the other holds that the risen Christ is there.

differences.heading: The Mass and the meeting house
differences.a: Scripture prescribes no fixed service, so each congregation builds its own around the Bible read and preached, prayer and song. There is no church calendar past Christmas and Easter, and no book in the pew to follow. The sermon carries the hour, the songs were picked this week, and the room points at the pulpit rather than at an altar.
differences.b: Worship is liturgical at the deepest end: a fixed order, a calendar from Advent round to Christ the King, and readings set years in advance, so Roman-rite parishes in Manila and in Munich hear the same Gospel on the same Sunday. Nobody present has to hope the man at the front is on form, because most of the words are Scripture.
differences.plain: In one church the words are the same everywhere that morning; in the other they were written this week.

differences.heading: Israel and the end times
differences.a: The Baptist reading leans dispensational: God's promises to the nation of Israel will be kept literally in a future earthly kingdom, and most expect the church caught up before a seven-year tribulation, which is what people mean by the rapture. No Baptist document requires any of it, but it runs through the preaching and the study Bibles this stream grew up reading.
differences.b: Catholics read one people of God across both testaments, with the promises to Abraham finding their answer in Christ and in the world He is making new. There is no rapture in it, and no separate programme running alongside the church. The Second Vatican Council said in 1965 that the Jewish people are not rejected by God, quoting Paul in Romans 11.
differences.plain: One expects a chapter still to be written for Israel; the other reads one story, one people.

beyond_the_compass.heading: The pope
beyond_the_compass.text: Catholics hold that the bishop of Rome is Peter's successor and the visible centre of the church's unity, and that he and the bishops teach with real authority. A Baptist church has nobody above it at all: it calls and dismisses its own pastor, owns its building, and the convention it funds can stop working with a congregation but cannot give it an order.

beyond_the_compass.heading: Mary and the saints
beyond_the_compass.text: Catholics honour Mary as the mother of God, the title the Council of Ephesus settled in 431, and ask the saints in heaven to pray for them, holding that honour is not worship and that asking a saint to pray is like asking a friend. Baptists pray to God through Jesus and hold that asking anyone else adds a step Scripture never shows.

story: Baptists did not leave the Catholic Church. They left a church that had already left it. England broke with Rome under Henry VIII; the Separatists then left the Church of England, holding a church to be a company of gathered believers rather than everyone in the parish; and John Smyth's congregation in Amsterdam baptised believers in 1609.

Rome answered the Reformation at the Council of Trent, which sat from 1545 to 1563. It defined justification in 1547, teaching that grace comes first and enables everything while the will freely cooperates and can refuse, and it defined transubstantiation in 1551.

Four centuries later the Second Vatican Council put the Mass into local languages and, in Dei Verbum in 1965, set out where revelation comes from. The Baptists had meanwhile multiplied on the American frontier, where the gospel was offered to whoever happened to be in the tent, and formed the Southern Baptist Convention in 1845.
on_a_sunday: At Mass everyone stands, sits and kneels together, hears the same readings appointed for that day in Roman-rite parishes everywhere, and comes forward to receive; the hour points at the altar. In the Baptist church the room points at the pulpit, a pool sits behind it, there is a band or a piano, a sermon that runs half an hour or more, and an invitation to come forward at the end.
did_you_know: The gifts rail puts these two the way round nobody expects. Catholic teaching leans continuationist: Lumen Gentium says the Holy Spirit hands out special graces among the faithful of every rank, and charismatic renewal has been in Catholic parishes since 1967. The Baptists drawn here lean the other way.
